(i) the majority of the network models proposed in literature are based on random network models; (ii) the topological features reported in empirical studies are different from those of the random networks; (iii) there is a lack of a comprehensive framework to model the growth of SCN topologies, as reported in empirical studies; and (iv) the proposed perspective is expected to address the limitations of the existing network models.

(1) the network science approach is a promising tool to model the topology and robustiness of SCNs; and (2) the fitness based generative models are able to mimic the observed SCN topologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel network science approach that can realistically represent SCN growth and topological features, as reported in data driven studies.
the development of generative network models that can realistically represent the topological features of SCNs.
the development of network growth models that can realistically mimic the observed SCN topologies, in terms of the topological characteristics of real world SCN networks.

network science has the potential to provide valuable insight into the growth, structure, and robustness of real world SCNs.

the current state-of-the-art network models for SCN topological analysis and robustness assessment have been able to capture some of the observed topological features of real world SCNs; however, the existing models have been unable to capture the observed topological complexity of SCNs.

the existing network growth models are not able to mimic the observed topological features of real-world SCNs, and therefore, there is a clear need for the development of novel generative models, which can realistically represent the observed SCN topologies.
